To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) data collection and processing systems should be organized to support the knowledge discovery processes that are to take place, (2) the architecture should be designed to support data dissemination to multiple users and applications, and (3) the architecture should support data dissemination to a variety of user devices.

(a) data collection should be performed in a manner that is consistent with the knowledge discovery goals; (b) the data architecture should be designed in a manner that supports the knowledge discovery process; and (c) the data dissemination should be performed in an effective and efficient manner.

the design principles for big data are: 1) the data must be accessible and usable by all users; 2) the system must be able to scale to the needs of the organization; and 3) the system must provide an effective way to visualize and analyze the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How do we organize big data systems? What is the best way of collecting data? And how do we disseminate the results? We present our design principles for each of these questions.

big data is a complex problem that requires a systems approach, and the principles presented in this paper are meant to inform organizations on the systems aspects of big data.

the three principles presented in this paper should be considered when organizations are planning to implement a big data system.

organizations should focus on (i) data quality (i.e., data integrity, accuracy, and completeness), (ii) data collection (i.e., collection and storage of data, and (iii) data dissemination (i.e., the process of distributing data and knowledge derived from data).

organizations need to consider a number of design principles when architecting big data systems.
